newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran approves $7.5 bln issue of state certificates.
newsitem.headline: Iran approves $7.5 bln issue of state certificates.

text.p: Iran has approved the issue by various government bodies of $7.5 billion worth of state-guaranteed certificates, a newspaper said on Tuesday.

The daily Salam said the cabinet drew up the guidelines for the sale of 22.5 trillion rials ($7.5 billion) of "participation certificates", a substitute for interest-bearing bonds which are prohibited under Iran's strict Islamic laws banning usury.
The decision included guaranteeing the principal and a 20 percent annual return on the certificates, the newspaper said. It did not give the instruments' maturities or further details.

A number of state bodies, including city municipalities and regional and provincial development agencies, have issued the certificates to finance projects since 1994 when they were allowed for the first time since the 1979 Islamic revolution.
According to the scheme, investors become part-owners of the development projects and receive a provisional annual return of 20 percent.
Any extra profit would be shared among investors upon maturity, in line with the dominant view among Iranian Shi'ite Moslem scholars which bans the fixing of returns as tantamount to usury.
($1 = 3,000 rials at the official exchange rate)
